title: Relative flatness of explicit strict-perfect tensor terms
statement: Let f:X→S be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], U an open, L a strictly perfect complex on the open site over U [def-pc-perfect-complex], and G a complex of O_X-modules all of whose terms are affine-locally flat over f [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Each term of the explicit complex T [def-pc-strict-perfect-relative-tensor-complex] is flat as a sheaf of modules over (f inverse-image O_S)|_U [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. There are no derived objects, representative isomorphisms, degree intervals, quasi-coherence or nonempty-open assumptions.

source.place: Tag 0DJQ, local relative Tor calculation; Tag 08CI (2) to (1); original proof step 3; Tag 05NE, stalkwise flatness criterion

proof.text: Apply relative_flat_module_stalk to each G term at each x in U. It identifies its scalar-restricted stalk as flat over the base stalk without quasi-coherence. The inverse-image ring stalk is canonically the same base stalk. Restriction to the open site does not change these stalks.

The finite-free retracts of L remain finite-free retracts on stalks. Tensoring G with each retract yields a retract of a finite sum of flat base modules. Stalks commute with sheaf tensor and direct sums, so each total tensor term has flat base stalks. Flatness of a sheaf means exactness of tensor; stalkwise tensor comparison and detection of exactness imply this exactness on the localized open site. Empty opens and zero terms satisfy the same criterion.
